question: Will Russia and Ukraine hold any diplomatic meeting by November 30, 2026?
operative_rule: Official-capacity representatives authorized to negotiate Russia-Ukraine relations; an authorized mediator/interlocutor may qualify if governments know/authorize it. Must be in-person and publicly acknowledged by a government or credible-media consensus. Remote calls and proposals do not qualify.

new_facts.source: UK House of Commons Library briefing, Ukraine: A new push for peace
new_facts.browser_facts: The Commons Library said US-Ukraine-Russia trilateral talks in UAE were proposed and accepted in principle, expected in October 2026, but no date had been agreed and Russian attendee seniority was unclear. This is an official parliamentary briefing, not an original government announcement. It links the claim to ISW's Sep13 assessment; ordinary browser click to that page returned 403 (turn3216view0). No direct Moscow/Ukraine source URL was exposed in the briefing text.
new_facts.browser_capture_note: Browser page displayed publication date Sep15 and lines 26-46; exact browser fetch clock/raw body not retained.

new_facts.source: Ukraine MFA spokesperson Heorhii Tykhyi briefing transcript, Oct7
new_facts.facts: Search index identifies the official transcript and date. Page fetch was denied; its statement/readiness wording was not verified, so no claim is attributed to Tykhyi here.

new_facts.source: The Wall Street Journal, Putin Floats a Summit With Trump and Xi to Discuss Ukraine Deal
new_facts.method: Original WSJ page opened through explicit link in public Daily Beast story; browser returned title/subhead and first paragraph only. No local raw HTTP body/hash or access bypass; exact browser fetch clock unavailable.
new_facts.facts: WSJ says people familiar with the discussions told it that Putin proposed he meet Trump and Xi next month to discuss Ukraine; its subhead says Zelensky would not be included. It describes a proposal, not a held meeting. The accessible WSJ excerpt does not show a confirmed date, agreement, or Russian official statement. Daily Beast displayed publication Oct19 05:13 EDT (09:13Z) and reported the proposal arose in an Oct9 Putin-Trump call; this is secondary chronology, not official confirmation.

source_access_note.russian_official: One ordinary GET to https://tass.com/politics/2199557 returned HTTP200, but its actual body was an unrelated Putin/Middle East story (raw SHA 5c812567636293d033bc5be175096377d85279f1d1dde044e25c916ed7f3d9d4; logs/deep_review_20261017/0342_diplomacy_deltas_1200/tass_kremlin_consultations.body.json.gz). Do not attribute a current Kremlin statement from that response.
source_access_note.kremlin: Direct Kremlin-news-index request started 11:55:34Z, stalled, and was terminated without HTTP status/body; intent only at logs/deep_review_20261017/0342_current_official_1154/kremlin_news.intent.json. No repeated attempt.
source_access_note.scope: These bounded sources do not establish whether any other qualifying in-person meeting occurred after creation; failed/inaccessible pages are not evidence of absence.

existing_context: Preserve prior work/0342_ru_ukraine_meeting_facts.json and work/0342_current_meeting_followup_1156.json. Feb/early-Sep meetings predate Oct9 Gamma creation; Oct18 Ukraine page describes a phone call and a Ukraine-US meeting, not Russian attendance. Frozen description has an end deadline but no express start date; this packet makes no adjudication about pre-creation events.
conclusion_limit: The Oct19 proposal is not itself a qualifying Russia-Ukraine meeting. No probability or decision judgment made.
